sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 6339.2 ± 76.5 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface labeling with membrane-impermeable SNAP-reactive fluorophores confirmed that the tagged receptor reaches the cell surface; no functional (signaling) assay result is reported in the ledger clip for this specific construct.
sites.rationale: The construct replaces the native mGlu4 signal peptide with the rat mGluR5 SP and appends HA+SNAP tags before the mature mGlu4 sequence; in canonical UniProt numbering this places the tag at the SP/ectodomain junction (after residue 32, before K33). Python confirms residue 32 = G and residue 33 = K. Membrane-impermeable surface labeling directly validates extracellular display of the tag. This is an independent paper and a different tag from L1, so it is reported as a separate site at the same junction. Full-length human mGluR4 expressed from pRK5 with a rat mGluR5 signal peptide followed by HA and SNAP tags immediately before the mature mGlu4 sequence, producing a membrane-anchored construct validated for surface labeling with membrane-impermeable fluorophores (PMC10699790).

sources.claim: All SNAP- and CLIP-tagged mGluR1 (human), mGluR2 (rat), mGluR3 (rat), mGluR4 (human), mGluR7 (rat), and mGluR8 (human) were generated with N-terminal signal peptide from rat mGluR5 followed by HA- and SNAP-tagged mGluRs or FLAG- and CLIP-tagged mGluRs in pRK5 vector as previously described ( 4 , 6 ).

MYC-mGlu 4 was generated using a synthetic oligonucleotide designed to insert the MYC epitope tag into the amino-terminal BstEII site of mGlu 4 after the signal peptide as in Han and Hampson (1999 ) and cloned into pcDNA3 at BamHI/Not1 sites. mGlu 4 , C1 and C2 constructs were generated by the introduction of a Not1 site by Site Directed Mutagenesis (Qiagen Quikchange II XL) between (T874–Q875).

literature_notes: L3 and L5 report C-terminal HiBiT/LgBiT fusions on full-length mGlu4, but the C-terminus (residue 912) falls within the intracellular span 848–912 and is therefore not an extracellular surface-tag site; these are recorded in other_positions. L4 reports a Flag-tagged full-length human mGlu4 used for signaling assays but states no tag position; without a pinnable junction it cannot be promoted to a site entry. L1 and L2 both converge on the same junction (after residue 32), the only extracellular N-terminal position available after SP cleavage; they are reported as two separate entries because they come from independent publications and carry different tags, consistent with the instruction to report every ledger-supported site.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal HiBiT tag fused to full-length mGlu4 to stabilise the mGlu2–mGlu4 heterodimer; residue 912 lies within the intracellular C-terminal span (848–912) and is not accessible on the extracellular face.
C-terminal LgBiT/HiBiT-tagged full-length mGlu4 co-expressed and purified for structural studies; same intracellular C-terminal position as L3.
